# Learning Goals: Calculate the Variance of a Sample

**Generated by:** Skill 02 — Learning Goals
**Workshop slug:** variance_sample
**Bloom's level:** Apply
**ARIVA format:** 10-minute workshop

---

## Intended Learning Outcome (ILO)

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

> **Calculate** the variance of a small dataset by hand, following the three-step process: subtract the mean, square the differences, and average the squared values.

---

## Why This ILO

"Apply" is the right Bloom's level because the Verarbeitung task asks participants to actually execute the calculation — not just describe it. Ten minutes is enough to build the intuition (Reactivating), understand the logic of each step (Informing), and successfully complete a small worked example (Verarbeitung). Asking them to "analyse" or "evaluate" the formula would require more mathematical maturity than a complete beginner can develop in this timeframe.

---

## How the ILO Maps to ARIVA

| Phase | What it does for the ILO |
|---|---|
| **A — Arrival** | States the ILO out loud: "by the end you'll be able to calculate variance by hand" |
| **R — Reactivating** | Surfaces the intuition that spread matters — the motivation for variance before the formula |
| **I — Informing** | Explains what variance measures and walks through the three steps with an example |
| **V — Verarbeitung** | Participants calculate variance for a small dataset (2, 4, 4, 4, 6) using pen and paper |
| **A — Assessing** | Checks conceptual grasp: "If variance is 0, what does that tell you about the data?" |

---

## Assessing Question

The ILO is checked in the final 60 seconds with this question:

> "If I told you the variance of a dataset is 0 — what does that mean about the data?"

A participant has met the ILO if: they can answer that all values are the same (no spread, every value equals the mean) — demonstrating they understand what variance measures, not just how to compute it mechanically.

---

## What This Workshop Does NOT Cover

To protect the 10-minute scope, the following are explicitly out of scope:

- **Standard deviation** — the natural next step; participants will ask; park it for a follow-up session
- **Population variance vs. sample variance** (n vs. n−1) — introduces unnecessary confusion at this level; use n throughout and acknowledge the distinction exists if pressed
- **Why squaring (algebraic proof)** — the intuitive reason (cancellation problem) is sufficient; a formal proof is out of scope
